title: [Bug] Streaming input: zero-token continuation crashes EngineCore (Invalid request status: RUNNING) — client-triggerable via temperature>0 chat sessions
body:
## Summary

A streaming-input (resumable) session **kills the entire engine** (`EngineDeadError`) when a continuation turn produces **zero output tokens** — i.e. the model samples a stop token as the very first token of the turn. The scheduler then finds the resumed request still marked `RUNNING` in the waiting queue and raises, taking down `EngineCore` and every concurrent request on the server.

This is a follow-up to #52471 (streaming-input depth costs); splitting the crash into its own issue because it is a distinct correctness/availability bug with a clean trigger.

## Severity

The trigger is **ordinary chat traffic**: multi-turn sessions with temperature > 0 (the default for conversational serving; e.g. gemma-4's own `generation_config.json` ships `temperature: 1.0`). A zero-token stop-finish is a normal, per-turn sampling outcome, so a long enough conversation hits it with high probability — and one unlucky sample from one user crashes the shared engine for everyone. We observed **9 engine deaths across 5 fresh instances and 4 configurations**.

## Traceback (v0.25.1, deployed)

```
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1304, in _process_engine_step
    outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn()
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 547, in step_with_batch_queue
    scheduler_output = self.scheduler.schedule(self._should_throttle_prefills())
File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 981, in schedule
    raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid request status: {request.status}")
RuntimeError: Invalid request status: RUNNING
```

The traceback is entirely within `EngineCore` → `Scheduler` — **no frontend frames**. It is reachable by any driver of streaming input (the native `AsyncLLM.generate()` async-generator interface, the `/v1/realtime` handler, or a custom router); our runs used a thin HTTP shim over `AsyncLLM.generate()`, but the shim is irrelevant to the crash.

## Trigger conditions (all three required)

1. **Streaming input / resumable session** — the request re-enters the update-and-requeue loop. One-shot requests are unaffected.
2. **A continuation turn generates zero output tokens** — the first sampled token is a stop/terminator token, so after the "discard last sampled token" step there is nothing left. Requires **temperature > 0** so a stop token can win the first draw; we hit it within 1–3 continuation turns at `temperature=0.7`.
3. **It is a continuation, not the first turn** — turn 1 of a fresh session never triggered it.

## Root-cause hypothesis

`Scheduler._update_request_as_session()` keeps `_all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and discards the final sampled token, on the assumption a finished turn produced ≥1 token. When the turn produced **zero** tokens (first sample was a stop token), this degenerates and the request is re-queued in a state the next `schedule()` pass rejects as invalid (`RUNNING` while waiting). This matches the "discard the last sampled output token" design described in the streaming-input blog, which implicitly assumes a token exists to discard.

## Reproduction

Open a resumable streaming session and drive two turns of a chat model at `temperature=0.7`:
- Turn 1: system preamble + a question + (in our case one image). Completes normally.
- Turn 2: a follow-up question appended to the same session. Within a few such continuation turns, one returns `finish_reason=stop` with 0 tokens in ~15–20 ms, and the engine dies on the next schedule.

**Negative control:** the identical turns at `temperature=0.0` complete normally, every time — isolating the zero-token sampling outcome as the cause (not request format; we also ruled out `max_num_batched_tokens`, `compile_ranges_endpoints`, and re-supplying the discarded stop token as text). A deterministic variant can be built by constructing a prompt where a stop token is the greedy first choice. Observed with a multimodal model; the mechanism is not image-specific and likely reproduces text-only. Happy to share our full runner script.

## Suggested fixes

1. Handle the zero-token completion in `_update_request_as_session()` (a turn that stops before generating leaves the session in a valid resumable state).
2. Make the scheduler's invalid-status check **fail the offending request**, not raise into `EngineCore` — a per-request error should not crash the whole engine (defense-in-depth regardless of root cause).

## Environment

vLLM v0.25.1 (cu129), gemma-4-31b-it (multimodal), TP=4, streaming input via `AsyncLLM.generate()`.
